comparator.name: Biomedical Sciences
comparator.sourceNotes: Current official prospective year pages specify a coherent 60+60+60 EC framework. The 2026–2027 OER confirms its components and current formal rules; its year tables explicitly apply to the cohorts currently in those years, rather than guaranteeing unchanged regulations throughout a future entrant’s study. Appendix VIII p89 explicitly replaces the old 27-EC internship with the current 28-EC unit and changes minors from12 to11 EC. The visible current table and course specification pp35/62 therefore resolve the stale27-EC narrative. Two research minors remain genuine disciplinary choices, not a named formal route or invented specialisation. Free space totals7.5EC across years2/3. Mandatory0-EC RADAr is recorded separately, not added to180EC. Stage entry requires the full60EC first year plus40EC other bachelor components and an approved proposal; bachelor writing runs alongside it. Patient contact is educational biomedical contact, not a medical licence. Current formal conditions are not a promise of future offer.

core: Molecular, cellular and physiological mechanisms of human health and disease
Laboratory, clinical and population investigation of disease and prevention
Quantitative methods, evidence appraisal and biomedical research ethics
Patient-oriented research and evidence-based healthcare innovation
adjacent: Brain, cognition and neuroscience of health
Toxicology and chemical effects on health
questions: How do molecular and physiological processes produce illness and responses to treatment?
How do neural processes, perception and development relate to behaviour and mental health?
Which research evidence can improve patient care and prevention?

trace: introduces cells, molecules and organ systems as foundations for biomedical explanation

Complementary empirical tool: cleaning, manipulating and visualising tabular, spatial and text data, with a cross-disciplinary research project. Biomedical datasets and patient contact are not guaranteed.
studies population patterns, disease risk and prevention through epidemiological evidence
introduces the biological and psychological study of brain and behaviour
develops cellular mechanisms, including processes central to molecular disease biology
provides hands-on biochemical and molecular laboratory techniques, including work with blood and microbes
provides mathematical foundations for the later probability and statistics course
examines regulation and functioning of adult human organ systems
studies proteins, nucleic acids and metabolic reactions underlying cell function
explains pharmacological action, therapeutic effects and toxicity of drugs

Direct quantitative method: multivariate statistical modelling, linear/logistic regression, factor analysis, ANOVA/ANCOVA and non-parametric testing support biomedical evidence analysis. The actual enriched content is statistical modelling; the title does not establish a separate experimental-design syllabus.

Direct human anatomy and function: body systems, surface anatomy, imaging, spatial reasoning and dissection-related academic encounters support biomedical mechanisms. These are academic learning experiences, not clinical-skills training.
studies pathogens, immune recognition and innate and adaptive defence
compares normal physiology with disease mechanisms across cardiovascular, respiratory and other organ systems
explores the neurobiology that underlies behaviour and physiological response
examines human molecular pathology, genetics, inflammation and neoplasia

Complementary quantitative tool: regression, classification, resampling, shrinkage, tree methods, support-vector machines and clustering support predictive analysis. The course is general machine learning, not a biomedical bioinformatics sequence.
develops probability distributions, estimation and simulation for quantitative research
examines biological, psychological and social determinants of illness and health interventions

Direct evidence-synthesis method: systematic review and meta-analysis using R estimate effects and compare evidence across studies. It does not supply a new primary biomedical experiment or the extended research internship.
studies psychological development across the lifespan, including interactions among developmental influences
studies sensory processing and neural control of action with cognitive-neuroscience methods

Complementary normative method: moral theories, responsibility and reasoned judgments support appraisal of biomedical choices. The actual practical cases are general ethics, not a dedicated biomedical research-integrity or clinical-ethics course.
Complementary conceptual foundation: knowledge, consciousness and philosophical argument prepare for the mind/emotion strand, rather than adding biomedical laboratory content.

Complementary conceptual inquiry: consciousness, personal identity, neurobiological explanations of mind and perceptual experience deepen the neuroscience route without substituting for experimental neuroscience.
examines mental disorders across the lifespan through biological, psychological and social explanations
develops advanced neurophysiology, neuroanatomy and cognitive-neuroscience experiment design
studies neural and psychological mechanisms of language processing
Complementary conceptual inquiry into emotions, rationality, well-being and moral judgment; this supports the neuroscience/mental-health question without claiming a clinical treatment course.

alternatives.label: Biomedical mechanisms & health research
alternatives.concept: A biomedical route through molecular and cellular mechanisms, human physiology and anatomy, pathology, pharmacology and immune defence, supported by laboratory practice, epidemiology, quantitative analysis and evidence synthesis. Behavioural and cognitive study contributes to health and development. It does not reproduce Radboud’s longitudinal patient contact, healthcare-innovation projects, two specialist minors or required extended research internship.
alternatives.labelReason: A biomedical route through molecular and cellular mechanisms, human physiology and anatomy, pathology, pharmacology and immune defence, supported by laboratory practice, epidemiology, quantitative analysis and evidence synthesis. Behavioural and cognitive study contributes to health and development. It does not reproduce Radboud’s longitudinal patient contact, healthcare-innovation projects, two specialist minors or required extended research internship.
progression: Life/health and brain foundations precede the relevant formal dependants. Molecular biology, biochemistry, physiology and anatomy support advanced disease and pharmacology study; data foundations precede machine learning, and brain study precedes cognitive research and evidence synthesis. Every formal prerequisite and assigned offering is independently checked. Advisory preparation is considered without inventing extra hard prerequisites.

alternatives.label: Neuroscience, cognition & health
alternatives.concept: A neuroscience and health route connecting neurobiology, perception and action, higher cognitive functions, language and mental health with physiology, molecular disease mechanisms, quantitative methods and evidence synthesis. Philosophy of mind and emotion supplies a specific conceptual complement. It retains substantial biomedical study while giving less weight to epidemiology, immunology and laboratory training than the first route. It does not reproduce Radboud’s continuous clinical-context training or required internship.
alternatives.labelReason: A neuroscience and health route connecting neurobiology, perception and action, higher cognitive functions, language and mental health with physiology, molecular disease mechanisms, quantitative methods and evidence synthesis. Philosophy of mind and emotion supplies a specific conceptual complement. It retains substantial biomedical study while giving less weight to epidemiology, immunology and laboratory training than the first route. It does not reproduce Radboud’s continuous clinical-context training or required internship.
alternatives.distinctness: Relative to the broad biomedical route, this programme replaces six courses in epidemiology, laboratory methods, immunology, mathematical statistics and biomedical ethics with philosophy of mind and emotion, higher cognitive functions, psycholinguistics and abnormal psychology. These choices follow the evidenced neuroscience specialisation, not a numerical target.
progression: Life/health and brain foundations precede the relevant formal dependants. Molecular biology, biochemistry, physiology and anatomy support advanced disease and pharmacology study; data foundations precede machine learning, and brain study precedes cognitive research and evidence synthesis. Every formal prerequisite and assigned offering is independently checked. Advisory preparation is considered without inventing extra hard prerequisites.

selection.assessment: The closest route has sustained molecular, cellular, physiological, anatomical, pathological, pharmacological and immunological study with laboratory, population and quantitative methods. The second retains substantial biomedical mechanisms while prioritising neural/cognitive processes, language and mental health, with a bounded philosophy complement. Both answer material defining biomedical substance under the CP119 distinction; neither mere coherence nor gap disclaimers establish that conclusion. Six genuinely different courses per programme follow these priorities. Epidemiology/population health is evidenced but the available course subset does not sustain a further distinct population-methods programme; human movement lacks a sustained biomechanical/exercise-methods sequence; health technology assessment lacks the required specialist economic-evaluation sequence; toxicology has pharmacological and molecular support but no sustained distinct toxicology programme. Do not fill these candidates with weak adjacency. Stop at two.

blocks: Both introduce cellular and bodily mechanisms as a basis for studying health; Radboud integrates this with its first-quarter theme.
Both examine cellular processes and biological mechanisms; Radboud also integrates heredity and behaviour in this quarter.
Both study physiological regulation and the functioning of human organ systems.
Both examine disease processes including abnormal cell growth; Radboud's quarter also covers life stages.
Both investigate human structure and movement; Radboud integrates circulation and neural systems as well.
Both examine infection and immune defence; UCR concentrates these subjects in one advanced course.
Both explain disease mechanisms across organ systems; UCR does not mirror Radboud's personalised-healthcare sequence.
Radboud requires a scientific research project. UCR's advanced cognitive-science course develops experiment design but does not reproduce the required project.

Partial quantitative-method correspondence: Radboud’s unit includes statistics and bioinformatics/big-data assignments; UCR develops applied multivariate models and statistical analysis. It does not reproduce the government-advice or biomedical-data sequence.

Partial laboratory-method correspondence: biochemical and molecular laboratory work, including proteins, blood, microbes and DNA, relates to the first-semester enzyme and genetic-laboratory assignments. Radboud also includes etiological research and other integrated work.

Partial data-method correspondence: the current Radboud research unit explicitly includes an introduction to data science and analysis of students’ own data. UCR supplies general data handling and visualisation, rather than the full biomedical practical line.

Partial epidemiological correspondence: Radboud includes a cancer-epidemiology assignment and critical appraisal alongside signal-transduction and muscle-activity tasks. UCR develops disease-pattern, risk and population-evidence reasoning; it does not reproduce the full integrated research unit.

Radboud’s advanced biomedical research unit includes bioinformatics/big-data and integrated assessment. UCR’s evidence-synthesis seminar is valuable research preparation but is not this primary biomedical research sequence.
Radboud integrates scientific questions and healthcare innovation. General ethics supports reasoning but does not reproduce this specialist line.

notes.text: Radboud integrates laboratory, clinical and population research throughout its biomedical programme and requires a 28-EC research internship plus innovation projects and two specialist minors. UCR offers substantial related biology, health and research methods, but these schedules do not reproduce that continuous specialist training or required internship.

audience.programmeDescription: The Dutch-taught Biomedical Sciences degree studies health and disease from molecules and cells to people and populations. It combines biomedical mechanisms, research methods, healthcare questions and regular contact with patients and professionals.
audience.comparisonExplanation: Two UCR routes offer related study in biomedical mechanisms and health research, or neuroscience, cognition and health. Radboud adds a continuous patient-contact and healthcare-innovation curriculum, two specialist research minors and a required extended research internship. The UCR routes develop related academic capacities and do not confer the same disciplinary qualification.
